medium: A careful naturalist botanical watercolor plate recording visible plant structure on quiet warm paper.
composition: Isolate the observed plant arrangement while retaining its branching topology, leaf attachments and flower orientation.
texture: Use precise transparent washes, delicate contour accents and fine directional strokes along observed veins.
palette: Retain natural source plant colors with restrained pigment saturation and paper-white highlights.
lighting: Preserve subtle source light modeling without dramatic cast shadows or glossy illustration effects.
detail: Render only visible botanical structures; add no invented roots, cross-sections, species names, scale bars or numbered labels.
